sentences.text: On the newest quarter the premise holds as a revenue statement: total revenue growth on a year earlier sped up from the prior quarter, and Data Center grew faster than the company while taking a larger share of revenue.

The quarterly acceleration is almost entirely Data Center, which supplied +102.5 percentage points of the +105.9% growth, so the company-level speed-up is a fair stand-in for the segment even though no Data Center figure for the prior quarter is in the record.
On a fiscal-year basis the same segment was slowing, its growth down 74.2 percentage points from the year before, so 'still accelerating' is true only on the newest quarters, not on the annual trend.

The claim says demand, but the record measures shipped and billed revenue, and the filing itself says production complexity has caused supply and demand challenges and revenue volatility, so revenue can lag or lead demand.

The step from acceleration to buying at the 2026-09-30 price is not carried by this claim alone: that price needs 13.4% a year for 10 years, far below recent growth, but it leans on holding a 65.2% operating margin, and 0 of 40 filers starting at this size grew that fast.
The record ends with the quarter ended 2026-07-26, and the 8-K of 2026-11-12 on the chief executive's resignation falls after it, so nothing here shows whether demand held after that.
Deferred revenue grew +215.1% against revenue's +105.9%, which points to customers paying ahead of delivery faster than revenue is being recognised.
Revenue rose in each of the 8 quarters, and the August 8-K describes securing land, power and shell for a large AI data center campus, consistent with continued build-out.
Against its SIC 3674 class the company's growth ranks 6 of 63 at a time the class median is 13.0%, so the acceleration is not an industry-wide tide.
Receivables grew +126.8%, faster than revenue, lifting receivable days to 59.6 from 54.1, so part of the accelerating revenue has not yet turned into cash.
The annual Data Center growth rate fell by 74.2 percentage points, and one quarter of re-acceleration does not show the multi-year trend has turned.
The filing names production delays and revenue volatility in data center systems, so a quarterly speed-up may partly reflect supply catching up rather than new demand.
Whether the next quarters keep year-on-year growth above the +105.9% just reached, or whether Q2 FY2027 was a supply-driven peak.
Whether rising receivable days reverse, which would separate collected demand from booked revenue.
Whether the 65.2% operating margin the price relies on survives, since at the industry 90th-percentile margin the same price needs 28.1% a year.

conditions.text: Quarterly revenue falling below the Q2 FY2027 level of $96.22B in a later 10-Q would end the run of sequential rises and contradict continued acceleration.
Deferred revenue dropping below its year-earlier $2.04B would remove the sign of customers paying ahead of delivery.
A results 8-K reporting the next quarter would show whether Data Center growth on a year earlier stays above the 100% line the corollary tests.
